clusters.name: Walter's move to Sorrel Valley, 1952–1953
clusters.reason: Around Walter's move across the country in March 1952 and the purchase of the orchard, within the year: June grew homesick and wrote daily to her sister Edna; Walter spent long hours out in the trees away from June; Glen began fights at his new school; Walter stopped writing to his brother Harlan after a quarrel over their father's land money; June kept to her bed for weeks that first winter; Walter and June had rows over money for new trees; by September 1953 June joined the church choir and her letters to Edna thinned out, and her anxiety began to ease. The shifts stack across the family in the months after the move, and no one else's shifts show in these months.

clusters.name: Walter's orchard failing, 1968–1969
clusters.reason: Around the orchard's failure in May 1968 when a late frost took the whole crop and the bank called in the loan: Walter began drinking heavily; he and Glen blamed each other over the loan; Glen and Marian took over the family's money and the talks with the bank; Glen's son Carl's asthma attacks worsened that winter; Nora began wetting the bed in April 1969; Ida had heart trouble found and was told to stop working. By October 1969 Walter stopped drinking and took work pruning other men's trees, and Carl's asthma eased once spring came. The shifts move through the family in the months after the orchard sold in October 1968, and settle by the spring of 1969.

clusters.name: Glen's job lost at the cannery, 1975–1976
clusters.reason: Around Glen's job loss in February 1975 when the Ridgeport cannery closed: Glen sat out of work most of that year in the truck in the yard for hours; he and Marian had loud fights at night over money; Marian took a second job cleaning offices at night; Nora stopped eating properly and lost weight that summer; Nora kept to her room and said little to her mother; Walter began drinking again after six years off it. By March 1976 Glen started driving a delivery truck for the feed store, and by June 1976 Nora was eating again and made the track team. The shifts move through the family in the months after the job loss, and settle by the summer of 1976.

clusters.name: Wilma moving into Nora and Hollis's house, 1990–1991
clusters.reason: Around Wilma's move into Nora and Hollis's house in January 1990 when she sold her farm: Nora and Wilma clashed over the children's bedtimes and meals; Hollis worked late and kept out of the kitchen rows; Hollis took his mother's side; Owen had tantrums at preschool; Wilma took over Lily's care; Nora's eczema flared on both hands; Nora and Hollis had rows most nights. By June 1991 Wilma took a flat in town, and by August 1991 Nora's eczema cleared over the summer. The shifts move through the household in the months after Wilma's move, and settle by the summer of 1991.

declined.reason: 1994: August 12–16, a wildfire came over the ridge and the valley was ordered out; the family slept three nights in the school gym and were allowed home with the house untouched. Four shifts in these days—Nora frightened and keeping the children in sight, Lily sick to her stomach, Nora and Hollis snapping at each other, Owen unable to sleep without a light—all settle within the week once the family was home. This is an acute episode around a real threat, not a period.

1996–1997: Two shifts count after removing those marked neverOpens. Tess began drinking most nights in October 1996; Nora phoned Tess every night worried for her. By June 1997 Tess stopped drinking and went to meetings twice a week. No event among these shows a change in who is in the family or in how a key member functions on a known date; not enough in the diagram to choose a reading.
